questions.q: What is the core question a vector database is built to answer quickly?
options: Which stored vectors are closest to a given query vector
Which rows in a table have an exact string match
Which users are currently logged in
Which documents were uploaded most recently, by file size
questions.explain: A vector database exists specifically to answer nearest-neighbor similarity questions fast, which is a fundamentally different core operation from a relational database's exact-match queries.

questions.q: What is a 'collection' (or 'index') in a vector database?
options: A folder on disk where raw PDF files are stored
A named container with a fixed vector dimensionality and distance metric, defined when it's created
A single embedded vector by itself
A user account with administrator permissions
questions.explain: A collection defines, upfront, the shape of the vectors it will store (dimensionality) and the similarity metric used to compare them — both set at creation time.

questions.q: What does 'upsert' mean in the context of a vector database?
options: Deleting a vector permanently
Inserting a new vector, or updating it if one with the same ID already exists
Sorting all vectors by similarity score
Exporting vectors to a CSV file
questions.explain: Upsert combines insert and update: a new vector is added, or an existing one with a matching ID is replaced.

questions.q: In the Qdrant console screenshot shown in this lesson, what does the 'PUT collections/demo1' call do?
options: It deletes the demo1 collection
It lists every existing collection
It creates a new collection, setting its vector size and distance metric (Cosine) at that moment
It queries the collection for the nearest vectors to a specific input
questions.explain: The PUT request in the screenshot creates a new collection named demo1, explicitly configuring a vector size of 1 and a Cosine distance metric as part of that creation call.

questions.q: Why is a vector database's distance metric configured once at collection creation, rather than chosen freely on each query?
options: Because query-time flexibility is a security risk
The metric is a property of how the collection compares stored vectors, and it must match the embedding model's trained metric — a consistent, fixed setting rather than something to vary per request
Because changing the metric per query would make searches faster
Vector databases do not actually support configurable metrics
questions.explain: Since retrieval quality depends on the metric matching how the embedding model was trained and evaluated, it makes sense as a fixed property of the collection rather than a per-query choice.
